comments.body:
## Root cause (proven) — the defect is DIAGNOSTIC, not behavioral

**Ticking an AC checkbox does NOT invalidate an attestation.** Confirmed empirically by
running `pass1.material_fingerprint` over a tick-only description pair: the hashes are equal.
`pass1._normalize_checkbox_state` rewrites `[x]`/`[X]` to `[ ]` before hashing (change 330c),
and it applies to every basis key.

The material basis is a single composite sha256 over exactly `ticket_id`, `description`,
`file_impact`, `children`, plus `file_impact_scope` when the scope is an explicit `none`.
**"AC" is not a component at all** — acceptance criteria live inside `description`. Every
staleness message nonetheless recited `description/AC/file_impact/children`, naming an input
the fingerprint does not have and never saying which input actually differed.

That is what produced the three contradictory reports:

- **846b (ticking was safe)** — correct, and now pinned by a test.
- **c6c9 (ticking WITH evidence prose invalidated)** — correct: the added prose is a
  `description` edit. The message could not say so.
- **1909 (plain ticking invalidated)** — a real residual cause the message hid. A **pre-330c**
  attestation hashed the RAW description. If it was signed while the boxes were already
  ticked, later un-ticking one leaves neither the normalized recompute nor the
  `attest._legacy_material_ok` grandfather (bug 96d1) able to match, so it reads
  `stale-material` with nothing materially edited. (Signed while UNticked, it survives ticking
  — the legacy basis is byte-identical to the normalized one.)

Discriminating experiment: the same composite was recomputed under both the normalized and the
legacy algorithm for tick-only, tick+prose, file_impact and children edits. Only the composite
distinguishes nothing; the per-component hashes distinguish all four.

## Fix — Gerrit change 1434

The basis now hashes each key separately (`llm/plan_review/material_diff.py`), and the
per-component fingerprints ride in the signed manifest as additive
`material-part: <name> <hash16> <size>` lines and on the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar. Design chosen
over replaying the event store to `signed_at`: `children` is derived from OTHER tickets'
`parent_id` at read time, so a replay would need a whole-store rewind, and compaction squashes
exactly the old events where legacy attestations live. The signed manifest is the only
trustworthy record of what the reviewer saw.

Before:

    stale-material: the plan was materially edited since review
    (description/AC/file_impact/children changed)

After:

    stale-material: the plan was materially edited since review —
    changed: description (4210 -> 4396 chars), children (3 -> 4)

Swept every attestation refusal surface, not just that one message: `stale-reopened` names both
timestamps; the claim gate's `unsigned` names both remedies; a relation-snapshot read failure at
signing time stops advising `sign-review` (which re-hits the same read) while every other abort
keeps it; `generation.py` names the changed dependency ids; `completion.py` forwards a child's
closure reason. `stale-code` and `stale-head` already named the drifted files and the two SHAs
and are unchanged. Surfaces left alone because they already forward the reason verbatim:
`_commands/gates.py`, `_commands/transition_close.py`, `llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`.

## No gate outcome changed

Every edit is inside the `reason` string of an already-failing branch or is an additive,
diagnostic-only manifest line. `manifest_material_parts` is deliberately lenient (a malformed
line is skipped, not raised) so a cosmetic field can never convert a staleness refusal into a
parse error. The composite fingerprint is byte-identical to before. Verified: a per-branch
`(valid, verdict)` assertion for `unsigned` / `not-closed` / `stale-reopened` / `wrong-kind` /
`stale-material`, plus `tests/unit` + `tests/integration` (8601 passed) and
`tests/e2e`/`interfaces`/`lib` (1484 passed). The three unrelated failures
(`test_coverage_reconstruction`, `test_jscpd_dup_heldout`, `test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger`)
reproduce on a pristine checkout of the same base commit — pre-existing tooling/environment
failures, not this change.

comments.body:
## Status: change MERGED, ticket held open by a verifier infrastructure loop

Gerrit change 1434 is **MERGED** on `main` (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved
comments). All acceptance criteria are met and ticked.

The close is blocked on the completion-verification gate, which failed twice — at the default
step budget and again at `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=1200`. Its own telemetry shows a non-progressing
loop, not an under-sized budget: `max_consecutive_repeat=131` on a single identical
`search_files` signature out of 260 total tool calls. Raising the budget only lets it loop
longer, which is why the second attempt failed identically.

`--force-close` was deliberately NOT used: it discards the completion attestation, and an
infrastructure loop is not a reason to drop a safety gate. Filed as bug
46a2-9c1a-d855-4706 (`brusque-tippable-sunbittern`), linked `discovered_from` this ticket.

This ticket stays `in_progress` until that verifier bug is fixed or an operator decides to
force-close it. The work itself is complete and landed.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Three agents on 2026-08-05 reported contradictory answers to "does ticking an AC checkbox
invalidate a plan-review attestation?". The contradiction is a DIAGNOSTIC defect, not a
behavioral one, and the empirical answer is now settled (see Findings). Every attestation
staleness message today names a fixed, partly-fictional list of inputs, so a reader cannot
tell which input actually changed and hunts for an edit that could never have been the cause.
The operator has approved fixing this broadly: wherever rebar reports an attestation error, it
must say WHAT CHANGED. That approval covers this ticket's whole scope, including the additive
manifest change described below.

## Findings that fix the scope (verified in this checkout)

- The material basis is a SINGLE composite sha256, built in
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` `material_fingerprint()` over exactly four keys —
  `ticket_id`, `description`, `file_impact`, `children` — plus `file_impact_scope` when the
  scope is `none`. Verified by reading `pass1.py:750-777`.
- AC checkbox STATE is normalized out of that basis by
  `pass1.py::_normalize_checkbox_state` (`pass1.py:741-747`, bug 330c). Ticking `- [ ]` to
  `- [x]` therefore does NOT invalidate an attestation. Confirmed by running
  `material_fingerprint` over a tick-only description pair: the hashes are equal.
- "AC" is NOT a basis component. Acceptance criteria live inside `description`. Every current
  message says "description/AC/file_impact/children", naming an input that does not exist.
- A pre-330c attestation hashed the RAW description, so after a tick neither the normalized
  recompute nor the `attest.py::_legacy_material_ok` grandfather (`attest.py:614-631`) can
  match, and it reads `stale-material` with no component actually edited. This is the residual
  cause the current message hides, and it reconciles observation 3 in the original report.
- `children` is derived from OTHER tickets' `parent_id` at read time
  (`relation_snapshot.py::live_material_children`), not from this ticket's own event log.
- The signed manifest ALREADY carries per-child/prerequisite pins —
  `plan-material-pin: <role> <id> <fingerprint>` parsed by `manifest.py::manifest_pins`
  (`manifest.py:428-457`) — so the signed child-id set is recoverable from any pinned
  attestation without any schema change.

## Approach

Add per-component fingerprints to the signed manifest and diff them component-wise on read.

Concretely:

1. New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py`. It owns the basis
   (`material_basis(ctx)`, which `pass1.material_fingerprint` now calls, so the composite and
   the per-component view cannot disagree) and `material_components(ctx)`, which returns
   `{name: (hash16, size)}` for each basis key. The `size` is a plain integer count of that
   component — characters for `description`, entries for `file_impact` / `children` — and it is
   load-bearing, not decoration: a 16-char hash is one-way, so without a recorded count the
   message could say only "description changed", never "4210 -> 4396 chars". A count discloses
   no content. `explain_material_change(attestation, ticket_id, repo_root)` returns the compact
   human clause naming the components that differ.
2. `manifest.py::build_manifest` emits one additive, deterministic line per component:
   `material-part: <name> <hash16> <size>`, sorted by name — exactly four whitespace-separated
   tokens including the prefix. `manifest.py` gains `manifest_material_parts()` to parse them
   back into `{name: (hash16, size)}`. The lines are additive, so an existing verifier ignores
   them and a pre-change manifest simply parses to `{}`. The prefix cannot collide with
   `manifest_material()`, which matches `startswith("material:")`.
3. `attest.py::compute_validity` calls `explain_material_change` for BOTH `stale-material`
   returns (plan-review at `attest.py:588-601` and completion-verifier at `attest.py:527-538`)
   and puts the named components in `reason`. It also names the reopen timestamp on
   `stale-reopened` and keeps the already-specific `stale-code` / `stale-head` wording (both
   already name the drifted paths / the two SHAs).
4. `attest_gate.py::claim_gate_check`'s `unsigned` message (`attest_gate.py:121-126`) states
   both remedies, because rebar cannot distinguish "never reviewed" from "review PASSed but
   signing aborted": run `rebar review-plan <id>`, or `rebar sign-review <id>` if a review
   already passed. `claim_gate_check` already forwards `compute_validity`'s `reason` verbatim,
   and `_commands/transition_close.py::_raise_plan_review_close_gate_error` and
   `_commands/claim.py` render that same string, so fixing the source fixes the claim gate, the
   close gate and `review-plan --status` together.
5. The sites that re-word or drop the reason instead of forwarding it are pointed at the same
   helper or made to carry the data they already hold:
   - `generation.py:265-269` and `resign.py:198-208` — replace the fixed list with the named
     components.
   - `generation.py:270-273` — "a dependency's plan material changed since the review" names no
     dependency, although the changed pin set is in hand; `resign.py:262-270` already names the
     ids, so this one is brought to parity.
   - `completion.py:178` — a child's closure-validity detail is currently
     `f"signature: {sig.get('verdict')}"`, dropping the reason that explains it; it forwards the
     reason too.
   - `_cli/_llm_commands.py:118-141` — a signing failure whose reason is a relation-snapshot
     READ failure currently renders the generic "run `rebar sign-review`" advice, which is
     wrong: a re-sign re-collects the same generation and hits the same unreadable read. It
     gets its own branch naming the reason and the real remedy. The branch is keyed on the
     REASON, not the event: `plan_review_sign_aborted` is the base-class event that also covers
     arbitrary terminal signing errors, for which `sign-review` remains the correct recovery.
     The discriminator is membership in `PlanRelationSnapshotError.REASONS` (the existing
     closed vocabulary at `relation_snapshot.py:26-33`: `store-read-failure`, `missing-target`,
     `ambiguous-reference`, `malformed-reference`, `reducer-error`, `canonical-id-mismatch`);
     every other abort keeps today's `sign-review` advice unchanged.
   - `attest_gate.py:166-167` — the docstring's verdict vocabulary omits `not-closed`,
     `malformed-phase`, `incompatible-phase` and the `stale-pin-*` values; corrected so the
     documented list matches what `compute_validity` can actually return.

   These were found by an exhaustive sweep of every attestation refusal surface. Surfaces
   deliberately left unchanged because they already forward the reason verbatim:
   `_commands/gates.py::_claim_gate_reason`, `_commands/transition_close.py`, and
   `llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`. `attest/opcert.py` and `signing.py` are also left
   alone: their verdicts are cryptographic (`mismatch` / `foreign_key`), not staleness, and
   already name the two keys or ids that differ.

Why this approach: the composite hash is one-way, so naming a changed component requires the
old per-component values, and the only trustworthy source for them is the SIGNED manifest —
anything reconstructed at read time could disagree with what the reviewer actually saw. The
alternative of replaying the event store to `signed_at` is rejected: `children` comes from
other tickets' state, so it would need a whole-store replay, and compaction squashes exactly
the old events where legacy attestations live. Adding the parts to the manifest is additive,
authenticated by the existing HMAC, and deterministic (no timestamps), so re-signing stays
reproducible.

Attestations signed before this change carry no `material-part:` lines. For them
`explain_material_change` degrades in two useful steps rather than falling back to the old
fixed list: it uses the signed `plan-material-pin:` child ids to report a `children` add/remove
diff when one exists, and when no component difference can be named it says so plainly and
points at the pre-330c normalization basis as the likely cause, with the remedy.

No gate outcome changes: every edit is inside the `reason` string of an already-failing branch,
or is a new additive manifest line. No branch condition, threshold or verdict value is touched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` (new) — the material basis, component hashing,
  and the diff/explain helpers.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — `material_fingerprint` delegates its basis to
  `material_diff.material_basis` so the composite and the per-component view cannot diverge.
  This also moves 24 lines out of a file sitting at 776 of the 800-line cap.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py` — extract `current_plan_context` from
  `current_material_fingerprint_impl` so the composite and the component view read the same
  state.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — emit and parse `material-part:` lines.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — record
  the same per-component fingerprints on the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar so `sign-review` can name
  the component too.
- `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json` and
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — the two places that document the basis as
  "description/AC/..."; corrected to the real key list.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — component-named `stale-material` reasons (both
  kinds); timestamp-named `stale-reopened`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py` — actionable `unsigned` message.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — forward the child-closure validity reason, not just the
  verdict.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — a dedicated render branch for a `plan_review_sign_aborted`
  signing failure that names the reason and the correct remedy.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — state plainly that ticking a checkbox is attestation-safe, and
  document the component-named staleness reasons.
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py` (new) — the tests below.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_sidecar_heldout.py` — its fake `sidecar.emit` gains the new
  keyword argument so the pinned emit signature stays accurate.

`pass1.py` sits at 776 of the 800-line cap, so the new hashing code lands in
`material_diff.py`; `pass1.py` is edited only to DELETE its inline basis construction and call
`material_diff.material_basis` instead, which leaves it smaller than before.

## Testing

- Happy path: an attestation whose `file_impact` changed reports a reason containing
  `file_impact` and NOT `description` or `children`; likewise a description-only edit and a
  children-only edit, one test each.
- Checkbox pin (330c): an attestation over a description whose boxes are then ticked reports
  `certified`, not `stale-material` — pinning the normalization that is currently only implicit.
- Legacy/grandfather regression: a pre-330c attestation (raw-description basis) over an
  unchanged ticket still reports `certified`, and one that cannot be grandfathered reports the
  "no component differs" wording rather than a spurious component name.
- Edge: an attestation with no `material-part:` lines and no pins still produces an actionable
  reason and never raises.
- Gate-outcome invariance: for each of the stale verdicts, assert `valid is False` and the
  `verdict` value is unchanged from the current code — the same inputs are still refused.
- The full existing suites `tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_material_grandfather_96d1.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` and `tests/unit/test_plan_material_pins.py`
  pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `material_diff.material_components(ctx)` returns `{name: (hash16, size)}` whose keys are
      exactly the `material_fingerprint` basis keys; verified by a test that asserts the key set
      matches and that changing one component changes only that component's hash.
- [x] `build_manifest` emits sorted `material-part: <name> <hash16> <size>` lines that
      `manifest_material_parts()` round-trips; verified by a round-trip test.
- [x] A manifest carrying no `material-part:` line parses to `{}`, and a malformed one is
      skipped rather than raised; verified by two tests.
- [x] A `stale-material` reason from `compute_validity` NAMES the differing component(s) and
      does not contain the string `description/AC/file_impact/children`; verified by one test
      per component, plus a repo-wide grep asserting that literal survives only in
      `material_diff.py`, which documents its removal.
- [x] Each named component carries its before -> after count in a fixed shape,
      `<name> (<old> -> <new> <unit>)`, where the unit is `chars` for `description` and
      `ticket_id`, `paths` for `file_impact`, `children` for `children`, and `fields` for
      `file_impact_scope`; a component whose count is unchanged but whose hash moved renders
      `<name> (<n> <unit>, contents edited)`, and one present on only one side renders
      `added`/`removed`. Verified by a test asserting `1 -> 3` appears for a file_impact
      change.
- [x] Ticking checkboxes only leaves the verdict `certified`; verified by a test that signs over
      an unticked description, ticks every box, and asserts `compute_validity` returns
      `verdict == "certified"`.
- [x] A pre-330c (raw-description) attestation over an unchanged ticket still returns
      `certified`; verified by a test.
- [x] An un-grandfatherable pre-component attestation returns a reason saying the component
      cannot be named, rather than naming one; verified by a test.
- [x] `stale-reopened` names both the sign and the reopen timestamp; verified by asserting both
      appear in the reason.
- [x] The claim gate's `unsigned` message names both the `review-plan` and the `sign-review`
      remedy; verified by asserting both substrings in the reason.
- [x] A signing failure whose reason is in `PlanRelationSnapshotError.REASONS` renders that
      reason and does NOT advise `sign-review`; verified by a test feeding
      `store-read-failure` to the renderer.
- [x] Any other `plan_review_sign_aborted` failure still advises `sign-review`; verified by a
      test feeding an arbitrary error string to the renderer.
- [x] A dependency-material change from `generation.py` names the changed dependency ticket
      ids, matching `resign.py`'s existing wording; verified by asserting the ids appear in the
      raised message.
- [x] No gate outcome changes: for every branch touched, a test asserts the same
      `(valid, verdict)` pair as before, and `pytest tests/unit tests/integration` passes.
- [x] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states plainly that ticking an AC checkbox is
      attestation-safe; verified by a grep for that statement in the file.

## Provenance

Three independent agent reports on 2026-08-05, recorded in the original description above.
Related: bug 858c-786a-13be-4332 (the close gate cannot express an N/A criterion).
